newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas ends narrowly mixed, still in range.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas ends narrowly mixed, still in range.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended narrowly mixed Thursday in sluggish trade, with a steady physical market holding paper in a narrow technical range, industry sources said.
May eased 0.1 cent to close at $1.90 per million British thermal units. June settled 0.3 cent lower at $1.967. Most other deferreds ended with modest gains.

"It's deadly quiet. There's no news, the weather is the same, and cash is flat. We're probably stuck here for a while," said one Midwest trader, noting cold Midwest and eastern temperatures this week helped firm the cash.
But few expected the winter-like cold to last, and with storage well-above last year, few saw much upside until better cooling loads kicked in.
Well-below normal weather was expected to dominate most of the eastern two-thirds of the nation into early next week.

Meanwhile, technical traders agreed the market was range-bound, with May trendline support at $1.87 and better buying likely at the recent lows of $1.85 and $1.825. Resistance remained at $2 and then at $2.045-2.05 and $2.10. limit any downside near-term.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices were talked steady Thursday in the low-to-mid $1.90s. Midcon pipes also were relatively unchanged in the low-to-mid $1.80s. Gas at New York city gate was talked between $2.40 and $2.50, also flat from Wednesday.
The NYMEX Henry Hub 12-month strip rose 0.2 cent to $2.109. NYMEX said 24,687 Hub contracts traded, down from Wednesday's revised tally of 29,069.
No Permian or Alberta natgas futures traded Thursday.

On KCBT, May finished unchanged at $1.77, while deferreds ended down by one-half to two cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 0.1 cent to 13.0 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 83 lots changed hands, down from Wednesday's total of 209.
